text.0_Paragraph: These are the words of the young Yosef Karo,
text.1_Paragraph: son of the honorable Rabbi Ephraim, son of the honorable Rabbi Yosef Karo, may their memory be a blessing:
text.2_Paragraph: I will greatly thank the Lord with my mouth, and in the midst of many I will praise Him, and with my songs I will extol Him.
text.3_Paragraph: How shall I come before the Lord, bow before the God on high, who from His holy dwelling from the heavens appeared in His abundant mercy and kindness, and bestowed His goodness upon a lowly man like myself, to compose a book that offers elegant words? I speak of the great work I compiled on the Arba'a Turim ('Four Columns'), which I titled Beit Yosef. In it, I included all the laws found among all the decisors, both new and old, with their dwelling places in their courts and their citadels, in the Babylonian Talmud and the Jerusalem Talmud, in the Tosefta, the Sifra, the Sifri, the Mekhilta, as well as the writings of the commentators, the decisors, and the authors of responsa, both new and old. Each law is clearly explained therein, each word properly arranged in its context, and the palace stands firmly on its foundation, with all the shields of the mighty hanging upon it, men of renown from ancient times.
text.4_Paragraph: I saw in my heart that it would be good to gather the sapphire lilies of its sayings in a concise manner and with clear, comprehensive, beautiful and pleasant language, so that the perfect Torah of the Lord might be fluent in the mouth of every Israelite. Thus, when a Torah scholar is asked a matter of law, he will not stammer, but will say to wisdom: "You are my sister!" Just as it is clear to him that his sister is forbidden to him, so will every law be clear to him when he is asked about practical application, since he will have this book fluent on his lips, built as a stronghold that all turn to. It is divided into thirty sections, so one can study a section each day, and thus review his learning each month; and it will be said of him: "Fortunate is one who comes here with his learning in hand."
text.5_Paragraph: Furthermore, young students will constantly meditate upon it and memorize its language, so that their childhood learning will be ordered in their mouths from their youth for practical application, and even when they grow old, they will not depart from it. The wise will shine like the brightness of the firmament; when they rest from their troubles and the labor of their hands, they will delight their souls by studying this book, which is entirely precious, containing definitive law, without unnecessary discourse or debate.
text.6_Paragraph: I have called this book Shulchan Aruch ('Set Table'), for in it the student will find all kinds of delicacies, properly arranged and preserved, orderly and clear. I am confident, through the grace of the Most High, that through this book the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the Lord—the small as well as the great, the student as well as the learned, the skilled craftsman as well as the one who understands whispers. Therefore, I spread my hands to the Lord, may He help me for the sake of His name's honor, to be among those who bring righteousness to the many, and may He grant me the merit to begin and complete it, so that it may be arranged according to His law, correct, accepted, good, and beautiful. And I now begin to do as I have promised, and may the Lord be my help.
